text.p: Following is a factfile on American Pete Sampras, who won his ninth Grand Slam title at the Australian Open on Sunday:
Born: Washington, D.C., United States, August 12, 1971.
1989: Upsets Mats Wilander to reach the fourth round of the U.S. Open.

1990: Reaches fourth round at the Australian Open and a month later wins his first tour title in Philadelphia. In September wins first Grand Slam title at U.S. Open, becoming the youngest player to enter the top 10, aged 19. Wins inaugural Grand Slam Cup. Finishes the year at number five in the rankings.

1991: Suffers a string of injuries early in the year. Best Grand Slam performance is at U.S. Open where he reaches the quarter-finals. Finishes the year on a high note, winning ATP World Championship in Frankfurt.
1992: Leaps to number two but loses U.S. Open final to Stefan Edberg.
1993: Reaches number one on April 12 and completes his best year ever with wins at Wimbledon and the U.S. Open. Also wins six tour titles. Runner-up at ATP World Championship.

1994: Wins first Australian Open, and second Wimbledon and ATP World Championship as well as another seven tournaments. Holds the number one ranking all year. The only player to win titles on all four court surfaces.

1995: Wins third Wimbledon and U.S. Open crowns, but his year is overshadowed by the illness of his coach and mentor Tim Gullikson who receives treatment for four brain tumours. Sampras breaks down in tears at the Australian Open when he learns of the diagnosis. Loses number one ranking to compatriot Andre Agassi after 82 weeks at the top. Regains the number one ranking later that year when Agassi is sidelined through injury.

1996: Sampras takes a short break from tennis after the death of Gullikson. He falls to number three after a shock third-round exit at Australian Open, but returns to number one less than a month later. Struggles in a five-set U.S. Open quarter-final suffering bouts of vomiting on court and dehydration. Incredibly wins the match and then goes on to beat Michael Chang in the final. Dedicates victory to Gullikson. Finishes the year by lifting ATP World Championship.
1997: Wins second Australian Open crown, crushing Spain's Carlos Moya in straight sets in the final.
